history.content: ok so this is gonna sound weird but i drove past my old high school today and instead of wanting to throw up i just felt. fine? which is somehow more upsetting lol
That shift from "wanting to throw up" to just feeling fine sounds strangely unsettling. I’m wondering if the upsetting part is how ordinary it felt.

nah not sad really. more like. huh. ok so backstory, i was kind of a disaster there. got my heart stomped, failed chem twice, the whole tragic teen package. used to drive ten mins out of my way just to avoid that road
Not sad, and more like a quiet "huh" makes sense after all that. Driving the same road after avoiding it for so long sounds like it carried a lot of history.

yeah and the dumb part is i think im actually relieved? like oh thank god that kid survived. but theres also this tiny weird grief thing like. that whole drama used to feel SO big and now its just a building i drive past. mourning my own teen angst i guess lmao
Relieved, and also that tiny grief about it being “just a building” now. That sounds like a real little mourning for how huge that time used to feel.

yeah thats it exactly. both at the same time. i guess it means im actually ok now which is what i always wanted? just didnt think being ok would feel a little like losing something. the kid took it all so seriously, bless him
Both at once, yes, relief and a small loss sitting together. I’m curious whether they feel side by side, or if the grief is tucked underneath the relief.
honestly the relief is on top and the grief is like. a little undercurrent. mostly its peaceful tho. like i can finally drive any road i want. didnt expect a random tuesday detour to do all that
That peacefulness, with the grief just underneath, feels like the main thing here. A random Tuesday detour ended up touching a whole old chapter.
yeah. yeah that about covers it. kinda nice to just say it out loud and have it not be a whole thing. anyway im gonna go take the long way home on purpose this time lol. thanks little guy
Go enjoy the long way home, that feels like a good place to leave it.
